bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# tailspin — A log file highlighter

tailspin highlights log files for easier reading. It can read from files or from stdin and supports printing
highlighted output to stdout or viewing interactively with a pager.

Usage examples:

- Read a file and view with the pager:
  tspin application.log

- Pipe into tspin and print to stdout:
  echo "hello" | tspin

- Follow a file (tail -f like behavior):
  tspin -f application.log

Installation:

- Homebrew: brew install tailspin
- Cargo: cargo install tailspin
- Package managers: check your platform's package repository

For more information, see the man page in the man/ directory (if present) and the example logs in example-logs/.

import subprocess, os, sys, shlex

def run(args, inp=None, env=None):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env: e.update(env)
    # ensure no config interfering: set HOME to empty tmp?
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, env=e)
    return p

# basic stdin
for inp in [b"hello world\n", b"INFO hello 123\n", b""]:
    p=run(["-p"], inp=inp)
    print("stdin -p", inp, "->", p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode)

# no args, stdin tty? piped empty
p=run([], inp=b"hello\n")
print("noargs pipe", p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode)

# file arg with -p
open("/tmp/test.log","wb").write(b"hello 123\nINFO test\n")
p=run(["-p","/tmp/test.log"])
print("file -p", p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode)

# nonexistent
p=run(["-p","/nonexistent12345"])
print("nonexist", p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode)

# invalid flag
p=run(["--unknown"])
print("unknown", p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode)

# invalid highlight color
p=run(["-p","--highlight","foo:bar"], inp=b"hi\n")
print("bad highlight color?", p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode)

# multiple files?
p=run(["-p","/tmp/test.log","/tmp/test.log"])
print("two files", p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode)

PY"}

import subprocess, os
def run(args, inp=None, extra_env=None):
    e=dict(os.environ); e["HOME"]="/tmp/fakehome"; e.pop("XDG_CONFIG_HOME",None); e.pop("TAILSPIN_PAGER",None)
    if extra_env: e.update(extra_env)
    return subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, env=e)

# JSON highlighter appears weird: in earlier default, JSON didn't apply; but maybe order? Let's test --enable json alone with various
for inp in ['{"key": "value", "num": 123}', '{"a":1}', '{"a": 1, "b": [1,2,3], "c": {"d": true}}', '[1,2]', '{"a": "b"} trailing', 'prefix {"a": 1}']:
    p=run(["-p","--enable","json"], inp=(inp+"\n").encode())
    print("json only", repr(inp), "->", repr(p.stdout.decode()))
# what about default JSON detection? maybe whole line must be JSON? Earlier sample: with json,numbers enabled, output was NOT json styled? {"a": 1} stayed except number. So json parser only if line is valid JSON?? Test whole line json in default mode:
for inp in ['{"key": "value", "num": 123}', '{"a": 1}', '[1,2,3]', '123', '"hello"', 'true', '{"a": [1,2]}']:
    p=run(["-p"], inp=(inp+"\n").encode())
    print("default", repr(inp), "->", repr(p.stdout.decode()))

# quotes interaction: earlier --enable quotes alone gave no output for '"hello world"' ? Wait second test gave highlight. First test samples quotes gave nothing - maybe because ??? Let's re-eval
p=run(["-p","--enable","quotes"], inp=b'"hello world" \'hi\' "hi" `code` "unclosed\n')
print("quotes re", repr(p.stdout.decode()))
# maybe because earlier test dict included backtick causing shell? No python direct.
# It returned unhighlighted first time but highlighted second time with different input? Check exact
for s in ['"hello world"', '"hello world" \'hi\'', '"hello world" \'hi\' "hi" `code` "unclosed']:
    p=run(["-p","--enable","quotes"], inp=(s+"\n").encode())
    print(repr(s), repr(p.stdout.decode()))

# pointers: 0xdeadbeef highlights but 0x123 doesn't? threshold length?
for s in ['0x0 0x00 0x000 0x0000 0x00000 0x1234 0x12345 0x123456 0x1234567 0x12345678 0xabcdef 0xabcde 0xABCDEF']:
    p=run(["-p","--enable","pointers"], inp=(s+"\n").encode())
    print("ptr", repr(s), repr(p.stdout.decode()))

import subprocess, os, sys, time, signal
def env(extra=None):
    e=dict(os.environ); e["HOME"]="/tmp/fakehome"; e.pop("XDG_CONFIG_HOME",None); e.pop("TAILSPIN_PAGER",None)
    if extra: e.update(extra)
    return e
def run(args, inp=None, extra=None):
    return subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, env=env(extra))

# Help variations
for args in [["-h"],["--help"],["-V"],["--version"],["help"],["--help","extra"],["-p","--","-h"],["--","--help"]]:
    p=run(args, inp=b"hello\n")
    print(args, p.returncode, repr(p.stdout[:500]), repr(p.stderr[:500]))

# No file, stdin is pipe vs ... already determined prints.
# What if file is "-"? 
p=run(["-p","-"], inp=b"hello 123\n")
print("dash file", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout), repr(p.stderr))
p=run(["-p","--","-"], inp=b"hello\n")
print("dashdash dash", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout), repr(p.stderr))

# stdin detection: no -p but piped stdin -> should print (man says always true if using stdin)
p=run([], inp=b"hello 123\n")
print("stdin no -p", repr(p.stdout))

# File without -p: should go to pager. Default pager is less? Set TAILSPIN_PAGER to cat-like script to observe.
# Create a fake pager script that logs args and cats file?
open("/tmp/fakepager.sh","w").write("#!/bin/sh\necho \"PAGER ARGS: $@\" >&2\ncat \"$@\"\n")
os.chmod("/tmp/fakepager.sh",0o755)
# TAILSPIN_PAGER must include [FILE]
p=run(["/tmp/test.log"], extra={"TAILSPIN_PAGER":"/tmp/fakepager.sh [FILE]"})
print("pager via env", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout), repr(p.stderr))
# without [FILE]?
p=run(["/tmp/test.log"], extra={"TAILSPIN_PAGER":"/tmp/fakepager.sh"})
print("pager no placeholder", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout), repr(p.stderr))
# --pager flag override
p=run(["--pager","/tmp/fakepager.sh [FILE]","/tmp/test.log"])
print("pager flag", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout), repr(p.stderr))
# -p overrides pager
p=run(["-p","/tmp/test.log"], extra={"TAILSPIN_PAGER":"/tmp/fakepager.sh [FILE]"})
print("print overrides pager", repr(p.stdout))

# If pager command fails / not found
p=run(["/tmp/test.log"], extra={"TAILSPIN_PAGER":"/nonexistentpager [FILE]"})
print("bad pager", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout), repr(p.stderr))

# Default pager when less not? Check which less
PY"}

import subprocess, time
def cap(): return subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-p","-t","tspin"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
def kill(): subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t","tspin"], capture_output=True)
kill()
base="export HOME=/tmp/fakehome; unset XDG_CONFIG_HOME; export TERM=xterm-256color; cd /workspace; "
# exec finishes quickly - does less stay? does tspin exit after command completes and user quits less?
subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s","tspin","-x","80","-y","24", base+"./executable -e 'echo hello 123'; echo EXIT:$?; sleep 100"])
time.sleep(1.5); print("exec finished, in less:\n",cap())
subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","tspin","q"]); time.sleep(0.7); print("after q:\n",cap())
kill()
# exec with custom pager cat in tmux (stdin is tty so exec should run)
subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s","tspin","-x","80","-y","24", base+"TAILSPIN_PAGER='cat [FILE]' ./executable -e 'echo hello 123; sleep 1; echo second 456'; echo EXIT:$?; sleep 100"])
time.sleep(0.5); print("exec custom cat t0.5:\n",cap())
time.sleep(1.5); print("exec custom cat t2:\n",cap())
kill()
# exec with -p in tmux
subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s","tspin","-x","80","-y","24", base+"./executable -p -e 'echo hello 123; sleep 1; echo second 456'; echo EXIT:$?; sleep 100"])
time.sleep(0.5); print("exec -p t0.5:\n",cap())
time.sleep(1.5); print("exec -p t2:\n",cap())
kill()
# file follow in tmux with custom pager? earlier cat exited quickly. exec ??? 
# stdin tty but no args: what happens? It should wait for stdin input? Or show error/help?
subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s","tspin","-x","80","-y","24", base+"./executable; echo EXIT:$?; sleep 100"])
time.sleep(0.8); print("no args tty:\n",cap())
subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","tspin","hello 123 Enter"]); time.sleep(0.5); print("after typing hello:\n",cap())
subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","tspin","C-d"]); time.sleep(0.5); print("after Ctrl-D:\n",cap())
kill()
PY"}

    for ch in chunks:

import subprocess, os, re
def env():
    e=dict(os.environ); e["HOME"]="/tmp/fakehome"; e.pop("XDG_CONFIG_HOME",None); e.pop("TAILSPIN_PAGER",None); return e
def run(args,s):
    return subprocess.run(["./executable","-p"]+args, input=(s+"\n").encode(), capture_output=True, env=env()).stdout.decode()
def enable(*gs):
    a=[]
    for g in gs: a+=["--enable",g]
    return a

# Pair KV vs numbers on digit key
print("KV vs N 123=456", repr(run(enable("key-value-pairs","numbers"), "123=456")))
print("KV only", repr(run(enable("key-value-pairs"), "123=456")))
print("N only", repr(run(enable("numbers"), "123=456")))
# Processes vs Numbers using config to differentiate id style
open("/tmp/cfg.toml","w").write("processes={name={fg='yellow'}, id={fg='red'}, bracket={fg='blue'}}\nnumbers={number={fg='green'}}\n")
print("Pr vs N cfg", repr(run(enable("processes","numbers")+"["--config-path","/tmp/cfg.toml"] if False else enable("processes","numbers")+["--config-path","/tmp/cfg.toml"], "proc[123]:")))
print("Pr cfg only", repr(run(enable("processes")+["--config-path","/tmp/cfg.toml"], "proc[123]:")))
# URL query value with date/number/path/uuid etc: URL internal query val style is cyan; if Dates earlier than URL, date inside query value could break URL? Test URL + dates only (disable numbers etc via enable)
for gs,s in [(("urls","dates"),"https://a.com?d=2022-09-22"),(("urls","numbers"),"https://a.com?d=123"),(("urls","paths"),"https://a.com/a/b/c?x=1"),(("paths","urls"),"https://a.com/a/b/c")]:
    print(gs,s,repr(run(enable(*gs),s)))
# Dates vs paths: date inside path segments
for gs,s in [(("dates","paths"),"/2022/09/22/a"),(("dates","paths"),"a/2022-09-22/b/c"),(("paths","dates"),"/a/b/2022-09-22")]:
    print(gs,s,repr(run(enable(*gs),s)))
# IP vs dates: IP like date? 2022.09.22 no.
# UUID vs IP: a uuid could be interpreted as ipv6? no dashes.
# Pointer vs UUID: pointer within uuid? use token "0xdeadbeef-..." no
# KV vs dates/paths/urls etc: key is value where value matches other
for gs,s in [(("key-value-pairs","dates"),"k=2022-09-22"),(("key-value-pairs","paths"),"k=/a/b/c"),(("key-value-pairs","urls"),"k=https://a.com"),(("key-value-pairs","uuids"),"k=c66a5398-2aa5-11ec-8631-0242ac110089"),(("key-value-pairs","ip-addresses"),"k=192.168.0.1"),(("key-value-pairs","processes"),"k=proc[123]:")]:
    print(gs,s,repr(run(enable(*gs),s)))

use crate::segment::{push_plain, Seg, Segs};
use crate::style::Style;
use regex::Regex;

pub fn apply(text: &str, re: &Regex, style: Style) -> Option<Segs> {
    let mut out: Segs = Vec::new();
    let mut last = 0usize; // byte index up to which plain text has been emitted (as pending)
    let n_groups = re.captures_len();
    for caps in re.captures_iter(text) {
        let whole = caps.get(0).unwrap();
        let target_opt = if n_groups == 2 {
            caps.get(1)
        } else {
            Some(whole)
        };
        if let Some(target) = target_opt {
            push_plain(&mut out, &text[last..target.start()]);
            out.push(Seg::styled(target.as_str().to_string(), style));
            // plain text between target end and whole end will be emitted as plain before next target
            last = whole.end();
            // But if there is plain text between target.end and whole.end, it needs to be in out
            // before the next segment. Since last jumps to whole.end, we must push it now.
            if target.end() < whole.end() {
                push_plain(&mut out, &text[target.end()..whole.end()]);
            }
            // Edge: if target.start is inside whole and there was plain before target but after last,
            // that was already handled by push_plain(last..target.start) – but if target doesn't start
            // at whole.start and last < whole.start, plain includes pre-match text correctly.
            // However if last was set to previous whole.end, the pre-target intra-match prefix
            // is included in last..target.start above.
        } else {
            // Exactly one capture group defined but it did not participate:
            // the original replaces the whole match with the (empty) group text,
            // effectively deleting the match.
            push_plain(&mut out, &text[last..whole.start()]);
            last = whole.end();
        }
    }
    if !out.iter().any(|s| s.style.is_some()) { return None; }
    push_plain(&mut out, &text[last..]);
    Some(out)
}

- Input from file (incl. --follow with pager temp-file tailing), stdin
  (chunked UTF-8 handling), and --exec via sh

  input" && git log --oneline -2"}
